decisions.executionNote: Approach the left standing white bottle with open left gripper; small initial increments to preserve elbow configuration.
Translate left gripper toward the standing bottle's mid-body, keeping a horizontal side grasp and right arm parked.
Prior chunk was rejected before movement; halve approach increments to maintain joint continuity.
Continue the left-side approach, aligning the open jaws with the standing bottle.
Fine-align around the standing white bottle, close left jaws, and begin a small retention lift.
Lift the closed left grasp clear of the tabletop, then start carrying toward the left dustbin; verify retention visually.
White bottle is moving with the left gripper. Carry left at clearance height, slightly turning toward the bin.
Move the retained white bottle farther over the bin opening, stop lateral motion, then release.
Allow the released bottle to fall, then withdraw upward and turn the left gripper toward the central lying white bottle.
Reposition above the near white bottle, gradually pitching the left gripper toward a top-down grasp while maintaining clearance.
Continue gradual wrist reorientation above the lying white bottle; align the jaws across its long axis.
Bring the left tool nearly vertical above the near white bottle and lower toward a top grasp.
Fine-center the left jaws over the lying white bottle, close, and perform a short vertical retention check.
Lift the closed top grasp clear and begin a leftward carry; check that the white bottle remains between the jaws.
White bottle is retained above the table. Carry left while gradually relaxing the downward wrist angle for bin approach.
Continue carrying the retained white bottle toward the left bin, maintaining height and smooth wrist rotation.
Position the retained second white bottle well inside the bin footprint and open the left gripper after stopping.
The white bottle is now visible at the table edge rather than inside the bin. Reapproach from above to recover it.
Align above the edge bottle with the left fingers across its width, lowering gradually with the jaws open.
Shift slightly left and lower to the edge bottle body, close the left jaws, and lift gently to test retention.
Lift the recovery grasp without wrist rotation, then move toward the bin interior while checking the bottle follows.
Recovery grasp did not retain the bottle. Reopen and approach its body lower and slightly right for deeper jaw engagement.
Bottle shifted right during contact. Adjust the open left gripper rightward at the current height, then close and test a short lift.
The white bottle escaped onto the table. Lift the open gripper clear before repositioning above its new visible location.
Replan with smaller forward increments after continuity rejection, aligning above the shifted white bottle without descending deeply.
Ease the wrist away from its near-vertical limit while retracting slightly and centering over the white bottle.
Previous approach was rejected without motion. Halve increments to smoothly recover from the wrist limit.
Clear the bottle before shifting right; rotate the open jaws to match its diagonal axis rather than pushing it along the table.
Back away from the wrist limit with smaller increments and a less vertical grasp approach, moving toward the bottle center.
Fine-align the left grasp on the bottle body, close at a shallower depth than prior attempts, then test a short lift.
The bottle did not follow the short lift. Reopen and adjust the grasp slightly forward/right and lower while watching contact.
Advance the fingers a little farther around the white bottle with a shallower approach, then close without lateral motion.
Test the closed grasp with a gentle retreating lift, preserving wrist orientation and staying away from the forward joint limit.
The grasp was empty. Reapproach farther along the bottle with a shallower wrist angle so its body enters the jaws instead of only the end.
The bottle body now fills the jaw opening. Make a small lateral correction, close, and check a gentle lift.
The closed jaws remained above the bottle. Reopen and lower vertically for actual body engagement, without advancing along the table.
Center the body laterally between the lowered jaws, close, and lift straight up to check retention.
Reopen and retract slightly along the bottle from its neck toward the wider body, accounting for the forward fingertip offset.
Close at the body-centered position and lift vertically, checking actual bottle motion rather than gripper command state.
The jaws closed above the bottle. Lower the open gripper substantially but gradually, with a slight forward correction, to reach the actual body height.
Lower and center slightly right on the visible bottle body, close at this deeper engagement, then test a small lift.
The white bottle appears seated between both fingers. Lift and retreat gently with the grasp closed, preserving the wrist angle to verify retention.
Retention is visible. Carry the white bottle toward the left bin with no wrist rotation and with clearance above the table.
Carry the retained white bottle farther left and back over the bin interior, keeping its orientation fixed.
Move the whole white bottle clear of the bin rim, halt the carry, and release it into the opening.
Withdraw the open left hand from the bin while the right hand begins a gradual pitched approach to the lying green bottle.
Continue the right-hand sloped approach to the green bottle body, lowering as the fingers pitch downward; keep the left arm clear.
Fine-align and close the right gripper on the green bottle body, then test a short lift while the left hand returns clear.
Lift the green bottle with the right hand and bring it toward a central handover; orient the open left hand to receive from its own side.
The previous chunk moved neither arm. Halve the left-arm increments while lifting the right grasp toward handover clearance.
Green bottle follows the right grasp. Bring it nearer the center and advance the left receiving hand with clear separation.
Align the left receiving tool toward the bottle from its own side; right hand holds near the centerline without crossing.
Back the left fingers off the right grasp and move toward the exposed neck, rotating the receiving jaws for a side grasp.
Approach the exposed green bottle from the left with vertically opposed jaws, keeping the right holder stationary.
Close the left receiving grasp around the green bottle before opening the right hand; separate the right hand slightly to check transfer.
Transfer looks insecure: reopen and withdraw the left receiver while reclosing the right grasp to recover the green bottle.
Green bottle fell onto the central table. Separate the open arms and reorient the left hand for a recovery grasp from its own side.
Approach the now-central green bottle with the left arm, aligning an inclined grasp across its diagonal body; withdraw the right arm.
No motion occurred on rejection. Reduce combined wrist and translation increments to preserve continuity while aligning the recovery approach.
Continue left-side recovery approach, pitching the open fingers down toward the green bottle body while clearing the right arm.
Lower the left grasp onto the wider green bottle body, with a small rightward correction, then close while the right hand stays clear.
Allow the left grasp to finish closing, then lift the green bottle vertically and slightly left to check retention.
Green bottle remained on the table. Reopen and approach lower and farther into the body so it reaches the gripping surfaces, not only the tips.
Center the green body between the gripping surfaces, slightly relieve table contact, close, and test a small lift.
Lift the closed left grasp vertically, then begin a gentle leftward carry only after clearing the table; verify the green bottle follows.
The green bottle slipped free. Reopen, recenter on its shifted body, and lower slowly for a deeper left-side grasp.
Shift the jaw center toward the bottle in the wrist view, slightly relieve contact, and close while stationary before attempting another lift.
Bottle is centered between the fingers. Let the grasp settle and lift straight up without lateral acceleration to check retention.
The lift was empty. Reopen and descend farther to the actual bottle height, correcting the earlier overestimate of table height.
Close at the deeper body engagement, hold still as the jaws settle, and test a short vertical lift.
Green bottle rose with the closed grasp. Lift further with a gentle leftward retreat, keeping wrist orientation fixed.
Carry the retained green bottle left at clearance height, slowly turning it to fit within the bin footprint.
Continue the retained green bottle toward the bin, turning gradually and keeping its body clear of the table.
Move the entire retained green bottle above the dustbin interior, bringing its neck clear of the table-side rim before release.
Release the green bottle over the open bin, pause for it to fall, then withdraw the empty left hand upward and inward.
